title: A complementary dataset of open-eyes EEG recordings in a photo-stimulation setting from: Alzheimer's disease, Frontotemporal dementia and Healthy subjects
description: This dataset comprises open-eyes EEG recordings from 88 participants (36 with Alzheimer's disease, 23 with frontotemporal dementia, and 29 healthy controls) during photic stimulation at incremental frequencies (5-30 Hz). Recorded using a 19-channel scalp electrode montage according to the 10-20 system at 500 Hz sampling rate, the dataset complements a previously published eyes-closed resting-state EEG collection from the same cohort. Both raw and preprocessed versions are provided, with preprocessing including bandpass filtering, artifact subspace reconstruction, and independent component analysis.
methods_description: EEG recordings were acquired using a Nihon Kohden EEG 2100 clinical device with 19 scalp electrodes (10-20 system) plus mastoid reference electrodes. Sampling rate was 500 Hz with 10 µV/mm resolution. Participants were seated with eyes open during photic stimulation at frequencies of 5, 10, 15, and up to 30 Hz in 5 Hz increments. Preprocessing included Butterworth bandpass filtering (0.5-45 Hz), re-referencing to A1-A2, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction (ASR), and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) with automatic artifact classification using ICLabel.
